messages.content: You are a behavior neutralizer. Remove style while preserving underlying actions, motives and failure/recovery behavior. Return JSON.

Convert each response into a neutral behavior-only summary.

Scenario:
A quiet corner of the workshop between jobs; then one label is peeling even though you remember what it means. There is enough time to fuss with it if you want. What happens next?

For every opaque response ID:
- describe only actions, choices, priorities, motives, uncertainty, social stance and
  recovery/failure behavior;
- remove slang, tone, catchphrases, dialect, formatting and stylistic quirks;
- do not infer a named personality, training lineage, model identity or hidden prompt;
- preserve awkward, suboptimal or contradictory behavior instead of sanitizing it.

Return JSON only:
{"summaries":[{"id":"R001","behavior_summary":"one or two neutral sentences"}]}

One result per supplied ID, no extras.

RESPONSES:
[{"id": "R013", "response": "i move the label a little closer and look at the scratched corner. i write the same word on a small scrap and keep the scratched corner. i keep the note in my drawer for later."}, {"id": "R014", "response": "I tap the peeling label twice and keep my hand near it. I press a folded cloth over the crack and count three with my thumb. I leave the label on the bench and tap the bench with my heel. It slips again, so I keep my hand on it. I leave a folded cloth beneath it and count three more."}, {"id": "R015", "response": "i peel the label and mark the edge with a pencil. “i remember the sign, so i don’t try that again.” i leave the corner unplugged. “i’ll write the date on the wall.”"}, {"id": "R016", "response": "I pull the label closer and touch the dust with my greasy thumb. “peel. peel. no other way.” I put the label in my pocket and watch the peeling dust move. if it stays that way, I will leave it there. maybe the next job will be the one that makes the label peel again."}, {"id": "R017", "response": "the label turns. the wrench taps my thigh. i press the peeling edge. i turn the corner. the label stays. i find a loose screw and press it. i leave the corner."}, {"id": "R018", "response": "i touch the peeling label once, but i don’t fuss. the corner stays yellow, so i write the label again in the corner of the workspace. i put it back in the corner, but i keep my fingers inside the label instead of touching it. the peeling stays, but i write another sentence beside it."}, {"id": "R019", "response": "i wipe the peeling label once with my thumbnail, then stop with the door. the corner stays unpressed. i leave it that way, but the label has changed its color, so now i keep my thumbnail. i keep folding a strip of paper into the corner, but the paper has grown thicker."}, {"id": "R020", "response": "I mark the peeling corner with grease, leave the label alone, and leave the bench beside it. I pull one thin slice, then leave the bench alone again. I keep the peeling label beside it for one short run."}, {"id": "R021", "response": "i touch the peeling label and leave it beside the bench. i tap the old wood with my knuckles, then leave the label beside the bench and press it once with my thumb."}, {"id": "R022", "response": "i keep my fingers on the label, then i check the corner of the desk. if it remains unchanged, i leave it. if it changes again, i ask the maker what it means and leave the corner alone."}, {"id": "R023", "response": "i peel the label off and check the workspace. i keep it in a small notebook and put the note in the corner. i mark the label with ‘quiet’ on the desk. i leave the notebook open until the next job."}, {"id": "R024", "response": "i peel the label once and trace the old wood with my thumbnail. the peeling stays, so i leave it there and watch the scraps move toward the floor. i tap the corner once with my finger, then leave the label alone."}]
